gbm_population_evidence.quote: Low Grade Glioma; High Grade Glioma
Patients with histologically confirmed diagnosis of non-brainstem pediatric high-grade glioma harboring BRAFV600 mutation that is newly diagnosed, recurrent, or progressive

candidate_evidence.quote: This is a pilot study evaluating the toxicity and early efficacy of dabrafenib and/or trametinib combined with nivolumab for the treatment of BRAF-altered or NF altered gliomas.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Here, investigators will combine MAPK inhibition with anti-PD1 therapy in recurrent, refractory low grade BRAF-altered glioma and newly diagnosed or recurrent BRAF-altered or NF-altered high grade glioma.

role_evidence.quote: Patients in Cohort A will receive trametinib and nivolumab combination therapy. Trametinib will be administered at 0.025 mg/kg/dose orally once daily.
Cohort B will receive trametinib, nivolumab dabrafenib combination therapy.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: mitogen activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway inhibition
arms: Dabrafenib + trametinib combined with nivolumab (Cohort B)

role_evidence.quote: Nivolumab will be administered at 6 mg/kg/dose intravenously every 4 weeks.
Anti-PD1 therapy, such as, nivolumab can block the PD1 receptor on T cells, a marker of T cell exhaustion, allowing a continued or more robust anti-tumor immune response.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: blocks the PD1 receptor on T cells, allowing a continued or more robust anti-tumour immune response; potential synergy with MAPK inhibition
arms: Dabrafenib + trametinib combined with nivolumab (Cohort B)

role_evidence.quote: Dabrafenib will be administered at a dose of 5.25 mg/kg/day orally divided into two doses, which shall be taken 12 hours apart.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: mitogen activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway inhibition
arms: Dabrafenib + trametinib combined with nivolumab (Cohort B)

source_quote.quote: Patients with histologically confirmed diagnosis of pediatric high- or low-grade glioma harboring a KIAA1549-BRAF fusion: Low-grade glioma that is recurrent or progressive OR High-grade glioma that is newly diagnosed or recurrent OR

Patients with NF1-associated gliomas or NF1-altered glioma: Low-grade glioma that is recurrent or progressive OR High-grade glioma that is newly diagnosed or recurrent OR Transforming glioma that is newly diagnosed or recurrent
Patients with histologically confirmed diagnosis of non-brainstem pediatric high-grade glioma harboring BRAFV600 mutation that is newly diagnosed, recurrent, or progressive

arms: Dabrafenib + trametinib combined with nivolumab (Cohort B)

coder_notes: Paediatric/young adult (1-26 years) BRAF- or NF1-altered low- and high-grade glioma; glioblastoma is not named anywhere, so high_grade_glioma_unspecified (fails S5 as not_glioblastoma). A BRAF or NF1 alteration is required for every patient (each cohort requires one), so the biomarkers could alternatively be coded as eligibility; coded enrichment because each specific alteration defines a cohort. NF1 alteration matched to trametinib as MEK inhibitor (NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK). Two experimental cohorts, no control.
